mechanism_name: Reserved/unallocated eMMC region holding a golden reference image
how_it_works: Rockchip eMMC layouts always contain raw, non-GPT-partitioned space before LBA 0 usable data: sector 0 (MBR), primary GPT (sectors 1-63), the idblock/loader1 region at sector 64 (~2.5MB, holds idbloader.img read directly by the BootROM at fixed offsets 64/1088/2112/3136/4160), a Vendor Storage block (~256KB) used for OEM calibration/config data, small 'reserved1' and 'reserved2' gaps, a raw U-Boot ENV block (~32KB), and loader2 (trust.img / ATF+OP-TEE, ~4MB) before the first GPT-declared partition (typically 'uboot' or the boot partition) begins around sector 32768 (16MiB). Separately, Rockchip parameter.txt CMDLINE layouts can define vendor-specific by-name partitions (e.g. 'security', 'vendor_storage') that are not always exposed as /dev/block/by-name symlinks to Android userspace if the fstab/twrp.fstab omits them, or that only kernel/TEE drivers can see. The hypothesized mechanism: at BootROM/miniloader/U-Boot/trust stage (all of which execute before compiled-in first-stage init parses fstab and switch_roots into /system), a routine reads a cryptographic hash or a full reference copy of specific /system files (init.rc, or a whole small archive) from one of these raw/reserved regions and, if the live copy in the ext4 system image differs, overwrites the live copy before continuing the boot chain. This would explain reversion happening strictly at power-cycle time and before any Android-level process (including a boot_completed receiver) ever runs, since bootloader/trust-stage code executes prior to and independent of AVB, SELinux, and even first-stage init's own logic.
fits_observed_symptoms: (1) Write succeeds and is visible pre-reboot: fits -- a bootloader-stage restore would not touch the live filesystem until a boot actually occurs, so any edit is visible immediately after being written. (2) Survives unmount/remount within the same recovery session: fits -- remounting exercises only the kernel VFS/ext4 layer, not the bootloader/BootROM path, so nothing would trigger a hidden restore. (3) Reverts only after a real power-cycle: fits well -- this is the mechanism's strongest match, since idblock/loader1/loader2/BootROM code by definition only runs once per cold boot (a `reboot` from a running Linux kernel does re-enter the full BootROM->miniloader->U-Boot->trust->kernel chain on Rockchip, unlike, say, a userspace-only restart), which matches 'only an actual power-cycle reboot triggers the revert.' (4) boot_completed marker never appears in /cache: fits, but only trivially -- if init.rc content itself is restored before first-stage init ever parses it, the injected boot_completed trigger was never part of the executed init.rc at all, so of course no marker is written. This symptom does not distinguish this mechanism from any other pre-init-parse revert mechanism (e.g. an OEM first-stage restore baked into the compiled-in init binary, or a recovery-triggered restore) -- it is consistent with, not unique evidence for, a reserved-eMMC golden copy. (5) AVB/vbmeta disabled: fits -- this mechanism is explicitly independent of AVB verification, which is exactly why it would keep working even with flags=2 (verification disabled) and an unsigned vbmeta; it relies on the bootloader/trust binary's own logic, not on the Android Verified Boot chain. (6) /system is ext4, not squashfs: neutral-to-fits -- a raw-region restore mechanism could target either raw ext4 blocks (via direct LBA writes into the super/system region before mount) or files after an early ext4 mount; ext4 read-write mutability actually makes a 'reapply golden file' step easier to implement than it would be against an immutable squashfs image. (7) non-A/B device: fits -- a single golden copy in a fixed reserved region needs no slot concept, so it works identically on A/B or non-A/B layouts; the super metadata_slot_count=2 is a separate, unexplained data point that should be investigated independently (it may be vestigial from a shared AOSP/Rockchip build config rather than evidence of an active second slot).
known_precedent: No citable, documented case was found of a stock or OEM Rockchip RK3326 (or any Rockchip SoC) Android/Android-Go STB or projector firmware storing a golden reference copy of init.rc or other /system files in a reserved raw eMMC region and reapplying it at early boot as anti-tamper. The reserved regions themselves (idblock/loader1, Vendor Storage, reserved1/reserved2, U-Boot ENV, loader2/trust) are real and well documented by Rockchip's own wiki and open-source U-Boot tree, and are known to legitimately hold bootloader binaries, OEM calibration blobs, and TEE/trust images -- but none of the public documentation, forum teardown threads (XDA, Khadas, tweakradje, androidpctv), or the AOSP-derived rockchip-android/bootable-recovery source describes them being used to store or restore Android system-partition file content. The closest AOSP-standard analog with real precedent is the install-recovery.sh / recovery-from-boot.p mechanism (a binary patch stored in /system/etc that reapplies a stock boot.img at boot if it detects tampering), and Rockchip's own 'security'/RPMB-backed anti-rollback counters (used for AVB rollback protection and attestation keys) -- but both of those are standard, documented, Android-partition-resident mechanisms, not evidence of a hidden raw-eMMC golden-image cache, and are better evaluated as separate candidate items in this study.
likelihood: Low. The reserved regions and offsets are real and architecturally plausible as a hiding place, and the power-cycle-only reversion timing fits a bootloader/trust-stage actor unusually well, but there is zero documented precedent for this specific behavior on Rockchip or AOSP generally, and every observed symptom is equally well explained by simpler, better-precedented mechanisms (e.g. a custom compiled-in first-stage init/recovery restore baked directly into the ramdisk's init binary, or an OEM TXCZ watchdog/recovery service) that don't require positing an undocumented golden-image cache in raw flash.
test_procedure: All steps below are read-only against the raw eMMC (dd with `of=` always targeting a file, never a block device) so they carry no write risk. From the existing `adb root` Recovery shell: 1) Enumerate all exposed by-name nodes to check for undocumented reserved partitions: `ls -la /dev/block/by-name/` and also `ls -la /dev/block/platform/*/by-name/` if present -- look for names like security, vendor_storage, rsv, reserved1, reserved2, vendor_boot, misc. 2) Dump the GPT to find where usable partitions actually start: `sgdisk -p /dev/block/mmcblk0` (or `parted /dev/block/mmcblk0 unit s print`) and note the first partition's starting LBA -- a gap larger than the standard ~32768-sector (16MiB) idblock/loader/vendor-storage/ENV region is itself a red flag worth investigating further. 3) Dump the entire pre-GPT reserved region to a file for offline analysis: `dd if=/dev/block/mmcblk0 of=/data/local/tmp/pre_gpt_dump.bin bs=512 count=<first_partition_start_sector> skip=0` then pull it off-device with `adb pull`. 4) Search that dump (and any other reserved-partition dumps pulled the same way, e.g. `/dev/block/by-name/security` if it exists) for literal fragments of the pre-edit init.rc content: `strings -a pre_gpt_dump.bin | grep -F 'on boot_completed'` (or grep for a known unique line from the ORIGINAL init.rc before you edited it) using a tool on a workstation after pulling the file -- a match strongly supports this mechanism. 5) Do a differential capture: right after making the edit (pre-reboot), dump the full raw device (or at minimum every reserved/vendor region plus the super/system region) with the same dd technique; power-cycle reboot; boot back into Recovery and take an identical second dump; diff the two images anywhere OUTSIDE the known /system region -- any byte-for-byte identical reserved-region content across both dumps that also matches the ORIGINAL (pre-edit) init.rc text is the confirming signature of a golden-copy cache; if no reserved region contains init.rc-shaped content at all, this mechanism is ruled out. 6) As a faster gate before doing full dumps, disassemble/strings the idbloader.img and trust.img themselves (dumped via the same read-only dd approach from their by-name nodes or raw offsets) and grep for filesystem-path-like strings (`init.rc`, `/system/etc`, ext4 magic `0xEF53` superblock signatures) that would indicate the bootloader/trust stage does filesystem-aware work at all -- stock Rockchip miniloader/trust binaries normally only touch dtb/boot/recovery/parameter, so any ext4 or /system-path awareness in them is itself notable.
bypass_or_fix: If confirmed: the only fix that doesn't require reverse-engineering and re-signing a custom idbloader/trust binary is to patch the golden copy itself so it matches your desired init.rc, using the same offset identified in test step 3/5 (`dd if=<your_edited_init.rc_shaped_blob> of=/dev/block/mmcblk0 bs=512 seek=<offset> conv=notrunc` targeting only the exact byte range, never a larger span). This carries real risk (see risk_level) because a misaligned or oversized write into the idblock/loader1/loader2/Vendor-Storage/U-Boot-ENV region can corrupt the BootROM-readable header or the trust/TEE image and produce a device that no longer boots past BootROM -- recoverable in principle only via Maskrom mode, which this device's project memory already flags as requiring hardware access not currently available. The lower-risk alternative is to locate and disable the *code path* that performs the restore (patch trust.img/U-Boot to skip the check) rather than fighting the golden copy indefinitely, but that requires unpacking/repacking signed loader images with Rockchip's tools and is higher-skill, still non-zero risk. Do not attempt either patch until the confirming diff in test_procedure step 5 has actually located byte-identical content in a specific reserved region -- patching blind is how eMMC bootloader regions get bricked.
risk_level: Diagnostic dumping (steps 1-4, 6) is read-only and safe -- dd with `of=` pointed at a file cannot damage the source device, and pulling files via adb is fully reversible. The differential-capture step (5) is likewise read-only/safe on its own. Only the bypass_or_fix write-back step is risky: writing into idblock/loader1/loader2/Vendor-Storage/U-Boot-ENV raw regions can produce an unrecoverable-without-Maskrom brick if the offset, size, or header format is wrong; that step should only be attempted after the mechanism is positively confirmed and ideally after a full raw eMMC backup (`dd if=/dev/block/mmcblk0 of=<full_image> bs=1M`) has been taken and verified readable.
